title: Ramps (wild leek)
def: Ramps are wild leeks with two or three broad smooth leaves in spring and a strong onion-garlic smell.

use: Learn it as an identification first. Eat it only after you have matched every feature in person, ideally with someone who knows the plant, from ground that was not sprayed or beside a busy road, and start with a small amount. Check smell on every leaf. False hellebore and lily of the valley grow in the same woods and are deadly.
not: Do not eat it on a photo match or a single feature, and do not eat it if you cannot rule out its look-alikes.
alike: False hellebore (Indian poke): Big pleated leaves that wrap the stem in a spiral; wet woods and meadows. No onion smell. Sometimes mistaken for ramps. Deadly
Lily of the valley: Two smooth upright leaves, small white bells on an arching stem, red berries. Mistaken for ramps. Every part is deadly

call: If someone may have eaten it, call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222, or 911 for trouble breathing, seizures, or collapse.
